tested:
No profile existed for "vmxvfp" (Juniper vMX Virtual Forwarding Plane - the
companion node to juniper-vmxvcp above) - every vmxvfp image silently fell
through to GENERIC_KVM_PROFILE. Sourced from EVE-NG's own real vmxvfp.yml
template (rule #33/#43/#57, docs/reference/eveng-implementation/raw/templates/
vmxvfp.yml): cpu=3, ram=4096, 12 ethernet interfaces (fxp0, int, ge-0/0/0..9),
same qemu_options (pc/kvm/host-cpu) as vmxvcp. EVE-NG's own config-scripts
catalog (08-config-scripts-catalog.md) lists a dedicated driver for "vmxvcp"
but none for "vmxvfp" - the VFP is a headless forwarding engine with no Junos
CLI of its own; it never receives a day-0 config push (day0_channel
deliberately NOT set here, matching EVE-NG's own behavior exactly, not a gap).
It boots and is wired to its VCP companion purely via the ordinary "int"
interface (index 1) - an ORDINARY netplex link between two ORDINARY nodes, the
same mechanism used for every other inter-device cable; no special multi-node
topology feature is needed (confirmed by reading EVE-NG's own vmxvcp.yml/
vmxvfp.yml templates directly - each is just a plain two-interface-plus qemu
node like any other device in this file).

reasons.nic:
disk_bus corrected virtio -> ide (NPX-1101 burn-down, 2026-09-20, rule #59):
EVE-NG's own real vmxvfp.yml template declares no `qemu_disk_interface` field
at all - the same as vmx-17.2R1's template, which this file's own
test_family_splits_survive_the_single_source already pins to "ide" - so EVE-NG's
unqualified default (ide) is what applies here too. The previous "virtio" was
unexplained drift (likely copied from the neighbouring vmxvcp entry, which
genuinely IS virtio because its family key matches the file-naming table's
"virtide" token - vmxvfp has no entry in that table at all).

settings.notes: Forwarding Plane - requires VMX VCP companion, no day-0 config of its own
